meta.title: Carriage of passengers and goods
meta.summary: You will learn how the Rules require you to carry children, people in a truck's load body and bus passengers, and how to position, secure and mark a load so that it does not get in anyone's way or put anyone at risk.

p: A child in a car is far more vulnerable than an adult. The standard seat belt is designed for an adult's height, so during hard braking it can cross a child's neck or stomach. This is exactly why child restraints are needed.
The Rules prohibit carrying children under 12 unless there is a special child restraint or other means that allow the child to be belted in with the standard seat belt ⟦18⟧.
The rule is stricter for the front seat: a child under 12 may be carried there only in a special child restraint. A seat belt adapter is not enough for the front seat.
list: Back seat: a child seat (restraint) or another means for belting the child in with the standard seat belt
Front seat of any motor vehicle, including a truck cab: only a special child restraint
You must not carry a child in your arms, either in front or in the back. There is no exception for taxis
The text of the Rules sets the limit by age only (under 12). Height is not mentioned in para. 157: it only matters when choosing a restraint according to the manufacturer's instructions
From age 12, a child travels like an adult, but must always be belted in ⟦19⟧
lesson.tip: For the exam, remember this pair: “under 12” and “front seat: restraint only”.

p: Paragraph 156 lists the ways passengers must not be carried. The logic is simple: a person must be somewhere the vehicle's design protects and holds them.
A motorcycle or moped driver must themselves wear a fastened motorcycle helmet and must not take a passenger who is not wearing a fastened motorcycle helmet ⟦20⟧.
list: Outside the cab of a car, tractor or self-propelled machine; on a goods trailer; in a caravan trailer; in the load body of a goods motorcycle; and outside the seating positions on a motorcycle. Exception: the flatbed body of a truck or a box body
More people than the vehicle's technical specification provides for. The mass of the vehicle with people on board must not exceed the manufacturer's maximum authorised mass
An intoxicated passenger on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped
More people than there are seats fitted in a truck's load body
Children under 16 on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped

lesson.h: People in a truck's load body: who may carry them
p: Carrying people in a load body is a serious responsibility, so there are special requirements for the driver ⟦21⟧. The driver must be 25 years old, must hold category “C” and must have more than five years of driving experience specifically in that category. Overall experience driving a car does not count.
If, together with the passengers riding in the cab, there are more than 8 people in total, the driver needs categories “C” and “D”.

Buses have their own thresholds: subcategory “D1” (more than 8 but not more than 16 seats, not counting the driver) - from age 21, with at least three years of experience working as a driver, including at least one year on “C1”; category “D” - from age 23, with at least three years of experience, including at least one year on “D1” ⟦22⟧.
Vehicles with right-hand drive, or with special controls, including fully manual controls, must not be used as taxis ⟦23⟧.

lesson.h: Travelling with people in the load body
p: A flatbed body is fitted out under the Basic Provisions ⟦24⟧: seats are placed at a height of 0.3-0.5 m from the floor and at least 0.3 m below the top edge of the side, and seats along the rear or side must have sturdy backrests. For carrying children, the sides must be at least 0.8 m high from the floor.

Before setting off, the driver explains to passengers how to get in, get out and settle in the load body, and warns them: standing in the load body or sitting on the sides while the vehicle is moving is not allowed. The driver may move off only after making sure that the conditions for safe carriage have been met ⟦25⟧.
If the load body is not fitted out for people, only those who are escorting the load or travelling to collect it may ride in it. And only if they have a seat below the level of the sides ⟦26⟧.
The speed of a truck carrying people in the load body must not exceed 60 km/h ⟦27⟧. In built-up areas, a 50 km/h limit already applies to trucks anyway ⟦28⟧.
lesson.tip: You must not stand in the load body, even if you are driving slowly.

p: You may let people on or off only where stopping is not prohibited, and only after coming to a full stop. Move off only with the doors closed, and open them only after coming to a full stop ⟦29⟧.

Stopping is ceasing to move for up to 5 minutes, or longer if this is needed for boarding or alighting passengers, or for loading or unloading ⟦30⟧. So within the zone of sign 3.28 “No parking” you may drop off a passenger or unload the vehicle, but within the zone of sign 3.27 “No stopping” you may not.

The driver of a route vehicle lets passengers on and off only at a designated stop ⟦31⟧. For category M2 and M3 buses, the ban on stopping at route-vehicle stop areas and within 15 m of them does not apply ⟦32⟧.
The rules are strictest for organised groups of children, because a single bus carries many children at once ⟦33⟧.
list: A bus with at least two doors
An amber flashing beacon
The “Carriage of children” sign at the front and rear
A driver aged at least 25, holding the required category, with at least five years of experience working as a driver
No more children than there are seats
A convoy of two or more buses carrying children on roads outside built-up areas is escorted by special vehicles of the internal affairs bodies

p: A load is carried on vehicles designed for that purpose. On a bus, load and luggage are carried only in the luggage compartment ⟦34⟧.
The mass of the load and passengers, and the distribution of the load across the axles, must not exceed the manufacturer's figures ⟦35⟧. Overloading makes braking and handling worse.
The driver checks how the load is positioned, secured and covered, not only before the trip but also on the way ⟦36⟧. If the load has shifted or a strap has come loose, stop and fix it.
A load may be carried only if it meets all the conditions of para. 162:
list: Positioned and, if necessary, secured so that it does not endanger people or damage other people's property
Does not restrict the driver's view
Does not make the vehicle harder to control or affect its stability
Does not cover the headlights, lights, brake lights, direction indicators, retroreflectors, number plates or the country identification sign, and does not stop hand signals from being seen
Does not create avoidable inconvenience
lesson.tip: If the load's position cannot be corrected, you must not continue driving ⟦37⟧.

lesson.h: Size and mass include the load
p: Signs 3.11 “Weight limit”, 3.12 “Axle load limit”, 3.13 “Height limit” and 3.14 “Width limit” concern the vehicle's actual dimensions and mass together with the load. A vehicle that is 3.2 m high, with a load 3.8 m high, will not fit under a sign 3.13 marked “3.5 m”.
For sign 3.12, the load on each axle is checked, not the average. That is why a load is distributed across the axles in advance ⟦38⟧.
lesson.tip: Always count height, width and mass together with the load.

p: Other drivers can easily fail to notice a long or wide load. That is why it must be marked ⟦39⟧.

If a load extends more than 1 metre beyond the front or rear, or more than 40 centimetres beyond the side, measured from the outer edge of a position lamp, the “Oversized load” sign is fitted: a 400×400 mm panel with alternating red and white diagonal stripes on a retroreflective surface.
During hours of darkness and in poor visibility, a light is added: a white lamp or retroreflector at the front, and a red one at the back.

Vehicles longer than 20 m (including with one trailer) and road trains with two or more trailers are marked at the rear with the “Long vehicle” sign - a yellow rectangle with a red border (Basic Provisions).

Overweight, oversized and dangerous loads are carried under a special procedure set by the authorised transport authority ⟦40⟧. A vehicle carrying dangerous goods is marked at the front and rear with the “Dangerous goods” sign: an orange retroreflective rectangle 300×400 mm with a black border and markings showing the goods' hazardous properties (Basic Provisions, para. 9).
lesson.tip: Numbers for how far a load may extend: 1 m at the front or back, and 40 cm at the side. White light faces forward, red faces back.

keyFacts: Children under 12 are carried in a child restraint or with another means of belting them in with the standard seat belt ⟦1⟧
In the front seat, a child under 12 is carried only in a special child restraint ⟦2⟧
Children under 16 must not be carried on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped ⟦3⟧
People are carried in a load body by a driver aged 25 with category “C” and more than 5 years of experience in that category ⟦4⟧
Standing in the load body or sitting on the sides while moving is not allowed ⟦5⟧
A truck carrying people in the load body travels no faster than 60 km/h ⟦6⟧
Route vehicles let passengers on and off only at a designated stop ⟦7⟧
A bus for an organised group of children: at least 2 doors, an amber beacon, “Carriage of children” signs, a driver aged 25 or over with at least 5 years of experience ⟦8⟧
On a bus, luggage is carried only in the luggage compartment ⟦9⟧
A load that extends more than 1 m beyond the front or rear, or more than 40 cm beyond the side, is marked with the “Oversized load” sign ⟦10⟧
In the dark, a projecting load is marked with a white lamp or retroreflector at the front and a red one at the back ⟦11⟧
If the load cannot be positioned correctly on the spot, the driver must stop and not continue driving ⟦12⟧
mistakes: “You can hold a child in your arms on the back seat if it's not far to go.” Not allowed: a child under 12 needs a restraint or another means of belting them in ⟦13⟧.
“A 10-year-old can sit in the front with a belt adapter.” Not allowed: in the front, a child under 12 is carried only in a special child restraint ⟦14⟧.
“You can stand in the load body if you hold on to the side.” Not allowed: standing in the load body and sitting on the sides while moving are both prohibited ⟦15⟧.
“Any projecting load must be marked.” The sign is needed only when a load extends more than 1 m beyond the front or rear, or more than 40 cm beyond the side ⟦16⟧.
“If the load is securely fastened, it doesn't matter that it covers the number plate.” A load must not cover number plates, lights or retroreflectors ⟦17⟧.
“My vehicle is under 3.5 m, so I can pass under sign 3.13.” Signs 3.11-3.14 take into account the mass and dimensions together with the load.

questions.q: You are carrying your 9-year-old son. You have no child seat, but you do have a special device that lets you belt him in correctly with the standard seat belt. Where can he sit?
options: In any seat, since you have a device for belting him in
Only in the front seat, so the driver can see the child
Only in the back seat, belted in with this device
Nowhere: without a child seat, you cannot carry a child under 12
questions.explain: Another means of belting a child in with the standard seat belt is allowed, but in the front seat a child under 12 may be carried only in a special child restraint.

questions.q: Your 11-year-old daughter asks to sit next to you in the front seat. Under what condition is this allowed?
options: If she is in a special child restraint
If she is belted in with the standard seat belt through a special adapter
If the trip is only within the city and the speed does not exceed 60 km/h
If there are no free seats for the child in the back
questions.explain: A child under 12 may be carried in the front seat only in a special child restraint. The standard seat belt, even with an adapter, is not enough for the front seat.

questions.q: Your friend wants to give his 15-year-old brother a ride on the back seat of his moped. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if the passenger is wearing a fastened motorcycle helmet
Yes, but only outside a built-up area and in daylight
Yes, if the moped rider is over 18
No: the passenger must be at least 16
questions.explain: The Rules prohibit carrying anyone under 16 on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped.

questions.q: A driver is 24 years old, holds category “C” and has 6 years of experience. Can he carry people in a truck's load body?
options: Yes, his experience is enough
Yes, if there are no more than 8 people
No: the driver must be at least 25
No: category “D” is always required for this
questions.explain: People are carried in a load body by drivers aged 25 who hold category “C” and have more than five years of experience in that category. Category “D” is additionally required if there are more than 8 people, including passengers in the cab.

questions.q: Before setting off, two passengers in a fitted-out load body say they will stand by the front side to see the road better. What should you do?
options: Allow it, if they hold on tightly to the front side
Allow it, but drive no faster than 40 km/h and avoid hard braking
Allow standing only on straight sections, and make them sit for bends
Not set off until they sit down: standing in the load body is not allowed
questions.explain: The driver instructs passengers and warns them that standing in the load body and sitting on the sides while moving are not allowed.

questions.q: During hours of darkness you are carrying pipes that extend 1.5 m beyond the rear of the vehicle. How must you mark them?
options: With the “Oversized load” sign and a red lamp or retroreflector
With the “Oversized load” sign and a white lamp or white retroreflector
Only with a red flag on the end of the load; no sign is needed
With the “Long vehicle” sign and an amber flashing beacon
questions.explain: A rear projection of more than 1 m is marked with the “Oversized load” sign. During hours of darkness, a red lamp or retroreflector is added at the back, and a white one at the front.

questions.q: A load extends 30 cm beyond the outer edge of a position lamp at the side. Is the “Oversized load” sign needed?
options: Yes, any sideways projection must be marked
No: the sign is needed when the sideways projection exceeds 40 cm
Yes, but only during hours of darkness
No: a load projecting at the side is marked only with flags
questions.explain: The sign is fitted if the load extends more than 40 cm beyond the outer edge of a position lamp at the side. Even so, the load must still not obstruct the driver's view or handling.

questions.q: You are carrying boards on a trailer. They are securely fastened, but they cover the number plate and one rear light. Can you drive?
options: Yes: the main thing is that the load is securely fastened to the trailer
Yes, in daylight, when lights are not needed
No: the load must not cover the number plate and the lights
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights on the trailer
questions.explain: A load must not cover the external lights, retroreflectors or number plates. Position it differently.

questions.q: A school is looking for a bus driver for a trip with an organised group of children. Which candidate meets the requirements of the Rules?
options: 23 years old, the required category, 5 years of experience
30 years old, the required category, 3 years of experience
27 years old, the required category, 6 years of experience
22 years old, the required category, 4 years of experience
questions.explain: Organised groups of children are carried by drivers aged at least 25, holding a driving licence of the required category and with at least five years of experience working as a driver.

questions.q: Which of these passengers can you carry on the back seat of a motorcycle if they are wearing a fastened motorcycle helmet?
options: A sober 17-year-old passenger
A 15-year-old teenager
An adult who has been drinking at a party
No one: motorcycle passengers must be at least 18
questions.explain: The age limit for the back seat of a motorcycle or moped is 16, so you may carry a sober 17-year-old passenger wearing a fastened motorcycle helmet. Children under 16 and intoxicated passengers are not carried on the back seat even wearing a helmet: an intoxicated passenger can lose their balance and tip the motorcycle over.

questions.q: May people be carried in the load body of a goods motorcycle?
options: Yes, if they sit on the floor and hold on tightly to the side
No: a goods motorcycle's load body does not carry people
Yes, but only on a field track, not on a highway
Yes, if the load body has sides at least 0.8 m high
questions.explain: Para. 156 prohibits carrying people in the load body of a goods motorcycle, and in general anywhere outside the seating positions provided for by the motorcycle's design. The load body will not hold a person in place during braking or if the vehicle overturns.

questions.q: Your son is 11 and tall for his age: 155 cm, and the standard seat belt fits him properly. You have no child seat or other device. Can you put him in the back seat and belt him in with the ordinary seat belt?
options: Yes: above 150 cm in height, a child restraint is not needed
Yes, if you drive only within the city and no faster than 60 km/h
No: under 12, a restraint or another suitable means is required
Yes, but only in the front seat, where the belt fits better
questions.explain: The Rules set the limit by age: children under 12 are carried in a child restraint or with another means that allows the child to be belted in with the standard seat belt. Height is not mentioned in para. 157; it only matters when choosing a restraint according to the manufacturer's instructions.

questions.q: Your daughter has just turned 12. How may she be carried in the front seat of a car under the Rules?
options: Only in a child seat, until she is 14
She may not sit in front until she is 16
Belted in with the standard seat belt
She does not need to be belted in if you drive slowly
questions.explain: The special requirements of para. 157 apply only to children under 12. From age 12, a child travels like an adult passenger, but must be belted in: a driver does not carry passengers who are not wearing seat belts.

questions.q: You work as a taxi driver. A female passenger with her 5-year-old son gets in the back and says she will hold him in her arms: it is only a five-minute ride. There is no child seat in the car. What should you do?
options: Carry them: the mother is responsible for the child in her arms
Refuse: a child under 12 must not be carried in someone's arms
Carry them, but drive slowly and along minor streets
Put the child in the front seat and belt him in
questions.explain: A child under 12 is carried only in a child restraint or with another means of belting them in with the standard seat belt, and in the front seat only in a restraint. There is no exception for taxis, and you cannot hold on to a child during hard braking. Offer the passenger a car with a child seat instead.

questions.q: You are driving a truck whose cab has only front seats. Your 10-year-old son wants to come with you. Under what condition is this allowed?
options: If he is in a special child restraint
If he is belted in with the standard seat belt
If the speed does not exceed 60 km/h
Children under 12 are never carried in a truck cab, under any condition
questions.explain: In the front seat of a motor vehicle, a child under 12 may be carried only in a special child restraint. There is no exception for a truck cab.

questions.q: According to its technical specification, your car has 5 seats. Your friends ask you to take a sixth person, who will sit in the back on a friend's lap. Can you do this?
options: Yes, for a short distance, if you drive slowly
Yes, if all the other passengers are belted in
Yes, if the sixth passenger is over 12 and sits in the back
No: the technical specification allows for only 5 seats
questions.explain: The number of passengers is limited by the vehicle's technical specification. There is no seat or belt for a sixth passenger, and during braking they are a danger to themselves and to the people next to them.

questions.q: A passenger asks you to drop them off here, at the right-hand edge. Can you stop?
options: Yes, if getting out takes no more than one minute
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
No: sign 3.27 also prohibits stopping to let a passenger out
Yes: letting a passenger out does not count as stopping
questions.explain: The place where you want to stop is within the zone of sign 3.27 “No stopping”. You may let passengers on or off only where stopping is not prohibited. Drive past the sign's zone and drop the passenger off beyond it.

questions.q: A passenger asks you to drop them off here, at the right-hand edge. Can you stop?
options: No: sign 3.28 prohibits both stopping and parking
Yes: sign 3.28 prohibits only parking
Only a taxi with its meter running may do this
Yes, but letting the passenger out must take no more than 1 minute
questions.explain: Sign 3.28 “No parking” is posted here; it does not prohibit stopping. Stopping is ceasing to move for up to 5 minutes, or longer if this is needed for boarding or alighting passengers. So you may drop the passenger off.

questions.q: When may a driver move off after passengers have boarded?
options: As soon as the passenger has got in, even if the door is still open
When the passenger is holding the door with their hand
At once, if the door is on the pavement side
Only once all the doors are closed
questions.explain: A driver moves off only with the doors closed and does not open them before coming to a full stop. An open door can strike a pedestrian, a cyclist or a nearby vehicle, and a passenger could fall out.

questions.q: You are carrying 10 workers in a truck's load body, and two more are riding with you in the cab. Which categories does the driver need?
options: Categories “C” and “D”
Category “C” is enough
Only category “D”
Categories “C” and “CE”
questions.explain: People are carried in a load body by a driver aged 25 with more than five years of experience driving category “C” vehicles. If, together with the passengers in the cab, there are more than 8 people in total, categories “C” and “D” are needed. Here there are 12 passengers.

questions.q: You are 30 years old. You obtained category “C” 4 years ago, and before that you drove a car for 6 years. Can you carry people in a truck's load body?
options: No: you need more than 5 years of experience specifically in category “C”
Yes: your overall driving experience is more than 5 years
Yes, if there are no more than 8 people in the load body
No: people in a load body may only be carried by drivers aged 35 or over
questions.explain: What counts is experience specifically in category “C”, and it must be more than five years. You meet the age requirement (25 or over) and hold the category, but you do not yet have enough experience in it.

questions.q: How are seats fitted in the load body of a flatbed truck that carries people?
options: Fixed at a height of 0.1-0.2 m above the floor, with no backrests needed
Fixed level with the top edge of the sides, so people have a view
Fixed at 0.3-0.5 m from the floor, at least 0.3 m below the top of the side
Fixed at a height of at least 1 m from the floor, with backrests
questions.explain: Under the Basic Provisions, seats are fixed at a height of 0.3-0.5 m from the floor and at least 0.3 m below the top edge of the side. Seats along the rear or side must have sturdy backrests. This way a person sits securely and will not be thrown out over the side.

questions.q: Children need to be carried in the load body of a flatbed truck. How high must the sides be?
options: At least 0.5 m from the floor
At least 0.8 m from floor level
At least 1.5 m from the ground
The height of the sides does not matter if there is a tarpaulin cover
questions.explain: For carrying children, besides the usual seating arrangement, the load body's sides must be at least 0.8 m high from floor level. The driver must also meet the requirements of para. 151.

questions.q: The load body of a flatbed truck is not fitted out for carrying people. Who is allowed to ride in it?
options: No one: people are not carried in a load body that is not fitted out
Any passengers, if there are no more than 8 and they sit on the floor
Loaders, if they stand and hold on to the front side
Those escorting the load or travelling to collect it, sitting below the sides
questions.explain: Only people who are escorting a load or travelling to collect it may ride in a load body that is not fitted out. The essential condition is a seat below the level of the sides.

questions.q: You are carrying furniture in a load body that is not fitted out. The loader escorting it can only sit on a sofa, and the sofa is higher than the sides. Can he ride like that?
options: Yes: he is escorting the load, and that is the main condition
Yes, if he holds on tightly to the side the whole time
No: he must sit below the level of the sides
Yes, if you drive no faster than 40 km/h and do not overtake
questions.explain: A person escorting a load may ride in a load body that is not fitted out only in a seat below the level of the sides. On a sofa higher than the sides, he could be thrown out during braking or on a bend. Have him ride in the cab instead.

questions.q: How many people may be carried in the fitted-out load body of a truck?
options: As many as will fit, provided no one stands by the rear side
No more than the number of seats fitted in the load body
No more than 8 people, in any case
No more than 20 people
questions.explain: The Rules prohibit carrying more people than there are seats fitted for sitting in the load body. Any extra passengers would have to stand or sit on the sides, which is prohibited.

questions.q: When may a truck driver move off with people in the load body?
options: As soon as the last passenger has climbed into the load body
When the passengers knock on the cab
At any time, as long as you drive slowly and smoothly
After making sure that the conditions for safe carriage have been met
questions.explain: Before setting off, the driver instructs passengers on boarding, alighting and settling in the load body. But the driver may move off only after making sure that the conditions for safe carriage really have been met.

questions.q: You are travelling with a caravan trailer. The children want to sit on the sofa in the trailer during the trip. Can they?
options: No: people are not carried in a caravan trailer
Yes, if the trailer has seats with belts
Yes, on a road outside a built-up area at up to 50 km/h
Yes, if an adult travels in the trailer together with the children
questions.explain: The Rules directly prohibit carrying people on a goods trailer or in a caravan trailer. Nothing holds a person in place in a trailer, and the driver cannot see or hear what is happening there.

questions.q: Which car must not be used to provide taxi services?
options: One with an automatic gearbox
One with right-hand drive
One with a diesel engine
An estate car with a roof rack
questions.explain: Para. 151 prohibits using vehicles with right-hand drive, or with special controls including fully manual controls, as taxis.

questions.q: According to the manufacturer, your pickup truck's load capacity is 1 t. Can you load 1.4 t into it if “the springs can take it”?
options: Yes: the excess is less than half the load capacity
Yes, if you drive more slowly and brake gently
Yes, if the load is securely fastened and covered
No: this is more than the manufacturer's figure
questions.explain: The mass of the load and passengers, and the distribution of the load across the axles, must not exceed the manufacturer's figures. An overloaded vehicle takes longer to brake, handles worse, and its tyres and brakes overheat faster.

questions.q: The whole load has been placed by the rear side. The total mass is within limits, but the load on the rear axle exceeds the manufacturer's permitted figure. Can you drive?
options: Yes: only the total mass matters, and it is within limits
Yes, if you reduce your speed and brake gently
No: the load must first be redistributed across the axles
Yes, if you pump the rear tyres up to the maximum
questions.explain: Para. 160 limits not only the mass but also the distribution of the load across the axles. An overloaded rear axle takes weight off the front one, and the vehicle steers and brakes worse.

questions.q: When must a driver check how the load is positioned, secured and covered?
options: Before setting off and while driving
Only while loading
Only if the load extends beyond the vehicle's dimensions
Only on roads outside built-up areas
questions.explain: The driver checks the load's position, fastening, covering and condition both before the trip and on the way. If a strap has come loose or the load has shifted, stop in a safe place and fix it.

questions.q: You are carrying long boards inside the car. They lie on the front passenger seat and cover the right-hand window and the right-hand door mirror. Can you drive like this?
options: No: a load must not restrict the driver's view
Yes: the left mirror and the interior mirror are still visible
Yes, if the boards are securely tied to the seat
Yes, if you drive slowly and do not change lanes to the right
questions.explain: A load may be carried only if it does not restrict the driver's view or visibility. Without the right-hand window and mirror, you will not see a vehicle or motorcycle on your right when changing lanes or turning.

questions.q: You have put bicycles on a rack mounted on the tow bar. The rear lights are visible, but the bicycles cover the rear number plate. Can you drive?
options: Yes: the rear lights and direction indicators are visible
Yes, in daylight, if the bicycles are secured
Yes, if the number plate is partly visible between the wheels
No: a load must not cover the number plate
questions.explain: A load must not cover the external lights, retroreflectors or number plates. Position the bicycles so that the number plate is visible.

questions.q: You are carrying a heavy boat on a roof rack. On bends, the car leans heavily and pulls to one side. What should you do?
options: Keep driving, but more carefully and more slowly on bends
Carry the boat a different way: it is affecting the vehicle's stability
Switch on the hazard warning lights and drive on to your destination
Pump the tyres up harder, so the car leans less
questions.explain: A load must not make a vehicle harder to control or affect its stability. A heavy load high on the roof raises the centre of gravity and can cause the vehicle to roll over. Also check the permitted roof load according to the manufacturer's figures.

questions.q: You are carrying dry sand in the open load body of a tipper truck. It is blowing onto the vehicles behind you. What must you do?
options: Nothing: the sand is dry and light, so it causes no harm
Drive faster to pull away from the other vehicles
Stop and cover the load so it stops blowing away
Switch on the hazard warning lights and drive more slowly
questions.explain: The driver controls how a load is positioned, secured and covered, and a load must not create avoidable inconvenience. Sand in a motorcyclist's eyes or on a windscreen is a direct crash risk.

questions.q: You have put boards on the roof rails without tying them down: “it's not far to go”. Can you drive like this?
options: Yes, for a short distance along quiet streets
Yes, if the boards are heavy and will not shift on their own
No: an unsecured load can fall onto the road
Yes, if you do not go faster than 40 km/h
questions.explain: At the first braking or gust of wind, unsecured boards will fly off onto the road or onto the vehicle behind. A load is positioned and, if necessary, secured so that it does not endanger people or damage property.

questions.q: Which of these loads must always be marked with the “Oversized load” sign?
options: Extends 1.2 m beyond the front
Extends 0.8 m beyond the rear
Extends 40 cm beyond the side, from the outer edge of a position lamp
Extends 30 cm beyond the side
questions.explain: The sign is needed if a load extends more than 1 m beyond the front or rear, or more than 40 cm beyond the side, from the outer edge of a position lamp. Exactly 40 cm is not yet “more than 40 cm”.

questions.q: At night, a load extends 1.5 m beyond the vehicle's dimensions at the front. What must be fitted on it at the front, in addition to the “Oversized load” sign?
options: A red lamp or retroreflector
A white lamp or retroreflector
An amber flashing beacon
Nothing, if the dipped headlights are switched on
questions.explain: During hours of darkness and in poor visibility, a projecting load is additionally marked: with a white lamp or retroreflector at the front, and a red one at the back.

questions.q: What does the “Oversized load” identification sign look like?
options: A yellow rectangle with a red border and a retroreflective surface
An orange rectangle, 300×400 mm, with a black border
A yellow square with a red border and silhouettes of children
A 400×400 mm panel with red and white diagonal stripes
questions.explain: It is a 400×400 mm panel with diagonal red and white stripes 50 mm wide, on a retroreflective surface, fitted at the front, rear and sides of an oversized load. A yellow rectangle with a red border is the “Long vehicle” sign, an orange rectangle is the “Dangerous goods” sign, and a yellow square with children on it is the “Carriage of children” sign.

questions.q: Your road train with its load is 22 m long. Which identification sign is mandatory at the rear?
options: “Oversized load”
“Long vehicle”
“Speed limit”
None, if the load does not extend beyond the vehicle's dimensions
questions.explain: The “Long vehicle” sign is a yellow rectangle at least 1200×200 mm with a red border. It is fitted at the rear of vehicles whose length, with or without a load, exceeds 20 m (including with one trailer), and on road trains with two or more trailers.

questions.q: Who sets the procedure for carrying overweight, oversized and dangerous loads?
options: The driver, together with the consignor
A police officer at the scene
The authorised transport authority
The owner of the load
questions.explain: Such loads are carried under a special procedure set by the authorised transport authority. When the terms of carriage are agreed, a speed is also set that must not be exceeded.

questions.q: Your truck's height without a load is 3.2 m, and with a load it is 3.8 m. Can you continue along this road?
options: Yes: the sign concerns the vehicle's height, which is 3.2 m
Yes, if you drive slowly along the middle of the road
Yes, if the load is soft and can flex slightly
No: the overall height with the load is what counts
questions.explain: Sign 3.13 prohibits the movement of vehicles whose overall height, with or without a load, exceeds the figure shown on the sign. With your load it is 3.8 m, so look for a detour: the load could strike a bridge or a pipeline.

questions.q: You are carrying a wide panel on a trailer; with the load, the width is 2.7 m. Can you continue along this road?
options: No: sign 3.14 takes the width with the load into account
Yes: the vehicle and trailer without the load are already 2.5 m wide
Yes, in daylight
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
questions.explain: Sign 3.14 prohibits the movement of vehicles whose overall width, with or without a load, exceeds the figure shown. You need a detour. In addition, a load extending more than 40 cm beyond the side is marked with the “Oversized load” sign.

questions.q: Ahead is sign 3.12 “Axle load limit” (6 t). The total mass of your loaded truck is 10 t, with 7 t on the rear axle. Can you continue?
options: No: the load on the rear axle is 7 t, and the sign shows 6 t
Yes: on average, each axle carries only 5 t
Yes, if you drive slowly along the middle of the road
Yes, if there are no other vehicles ahead
questions.explain: Sign 3.12 prohibits the movement of vehicles where the actual load on any axle exceeds the figure shown on the sign. The average does not count: the rear axle carries 7 t against a 6 t limit. That is why a load is distributed across the axles in advance.

questions.q: Ahead is sign 3.11 “Weight limit” (10 t). Your truck's mass without a load is 7 t, and with the load it is 12 t. Can you continue?
options: Yes: the sign concerns the mass without the load, which is 7 t
Yes, if the load on each axle is less than 10 t
Yes, if vehicles cross one at a time and slowly
No: the mass with the load, 12 t, is more than 10 t
questions.explain: Sign 3.11 “Weight limit” prohibits the movement of vehicles and combinations whose total actual mass exceeds the figure shown on the sign. The mass with the load counts: 12 t is more than 10 t.

questions.q: You need to unload furniture by a building entrance; this will take about 20 minutes. Can you stop at the right-hand edge within the zone of this sign?
options: No: longer than 5 minutes already counts as parking
Yes: unloading is stopping, not parking
Yes, but only for the first 5 minutes, then you must leave
No: sign 3.28 also prohibits stopping for trucks
questions.explain: Stopping is ceasing to move for up to 5 minutes, or longer if this is needed for boarding or alighting passengers, or for loading or unloading. Unloading counts as stopping, not parking, so sign 3.28 does not prohibit it.

questions.q: An acquaintance asks for a ride standing on the step by the cab door of your tractor. Can you do this?
options: Yes, if he holds tightly onto a handrail
Yes, but only on a field track, never on a paved highway
No: passengers are not carried outside a tractor's cab at all
Yes, if you drive at less than 20 km/h
questions.explain: The Rules prohibit carrying passengers outside the cab of a tractor or self-propelled machine. A person could fall off the step under the wheels, especially on an uneven road.

questions.q: Where on a bus may load and passengers' luggage be carried?
options: In the aisle, if it does not block the exit
Only in the luggage compartment
On the back seats, if they are free
Anywhere, as long as the load is secured
questions.explain: Loads are carried on vehicles designed for that purpose, and on buses a load, including luggage, is not carried outside the luggage compartment. Bags in the aisle get in the way of evacuation and fly onto people during braking.

questions.q: Both drivers have stopped at the right-hand edge to let passengers out. Which of them stopped in accordance with the Rules?
options: Only the blue one
Only the red one
Both
Neither
questions.explain: The red vehicle stopped past sign 3.27 “No stopping”, that is, within its zone, where you may not even let a passenger out. The blue vehicle stands before the sign, where stopping is allowed. Passengers are let on and off only where stopping is not prohibited.

questions.q: In which of these cases may passengers be carried outside a car's cab?
options: On a goods trailer with high sides and seats
In a caravan trailer, if it has seats with belts
In the load body of a goods motorcycle, if it has sides
In the load body of a flatbed truck or in a box body
questions.explain: Para. 156 prohibits carrying passengers outside a vehicle's cab. An exception is made only for the flatbed load body of a truck and for a box body, and even then only if the requirements for fitting out the load body and for the driver are met. People are not carried on a goods trailer, in a caravan trailer or in the load body of a goods motorcycle.

questions.q: While driving, you notice that the load in the load body has shifted and is covering the rear lights. This cannot be fixed on the spot: a forklift is needed. What should you do?
options: Keep driving with the hazard warning lights switched on
Keep driving, but only during daylight
Stop and not continue driving until the violation is corrected
Drive on to your destination without overtaking
questions.explain: A load must not cover the external lights. If how the load is positioned does not meet the requirements, the driver must correct the violation, and if that is not possible, must not continue driving. Stop in a safe place and call for help.

questions.q: Which identification sign is mandatory on a vehicle carrying dangerous goods, and where is it fitted?
options: The “Oversized load” sign, at the rear only
The “Long vehicle” sign, at the rear
The “Dangerous goods” sign, at the front and rear
The “Road train” sign, on the roof of the cab
questions.explain: A vehicle carrying dangerous goods is marked with the “Dangerous goods” sign at the front and rear. This is an orange retroreflective rectangle, 300×400 mm, with a black border and markings showing the goods' hazardous properties. The procedure for carrying dangerous goods itself is set by the authorised transport authority.

questions.q: A bus with an amber flashing beacon is travelling ahead. It has yellow square signs with a red border and a picture of children at the front and rear. What does this mean?
options: The bus is broken down and is on its way to be repaired
The bus is carrying an organised group of children: be especially careful
The bus is on an urgent mission and must be given priority, like an ambulance
It is a learner bus, and the driver is still learning
questions.explain: Buses carrying organised groups of children are fitted with an amber flashing beacon, and the “Carriage of children” identification sign is fitted at both the front and rear. This does not give the bus priority the way a vehicle with a blue beacon and siren has, but children may appear on the road near such a bus.

questions.q: Ahead is sign 3.15 “Length limit” (10 m). The length of your road train with its load is 12 m. Can you continue?
options: No: sign 3.15 counts the overall length with the load, which is over 10 m
Yes: without the load, the road train is shorter than 10 m
Yes, if you drive slowly with dipped headlights on
No: this sign prohibits the movement of all trucks and road trains
questions.explain: This is sign 3.15 “Length limit”. It prohibits the movement of vehicles and combinations whose overall length, with or without a load, exceeds the figure shown on the sign. Yours is 12 m against a 10 m limit, so you need a detour. Other trucks shorter than 10 m may pass here.

questions.q: Ahead is sign 3.11 “Weight limit” (3.5 t). You are driving a car with a mass of 1.8 t, towing a loaded trailer with a mass of 1.9 t. Can you continue?
options: Yes: both the car and the trailer are lighter than 3.5 t on their own
Yes, if you drive no faster than 40 km/h
No: this sign prohibits the movement of any car towing a trailer
No: the sign counts the combination's total actual mass, which is 3.7 t
questions.explain: Sign 3.11 prohibits the movement of vehicles, including combinations, whose total actual mass exceeds the figure shown on the sign. The vehicle is counted together with the trailer and its load: 1.8 + 1.9 = 3.7 t, which is more than 3.5 t. Look for a detour.

questions.q: You hold a licence with subcategory “D1”. You are 21 years old and have worked as a driver for 3 years, including 14 months on a subcategory “C1” truck. Can you be allowed to carry passengers on a subcategory “D1” minibus?
options: No: passengers may be carried only from age 25
No: at least one year of experience specifically on “D1” is required first
Yes: your age, overall experience and “C1” experience meet the requirements
No: 5 years of experience in category “C” is required first
questions.explain: Carrying passengers on subcategory “D1” vehicles (more than 8 but not more than 16 seats, not counting the driver) is allowed from age 21, with at least 3 years of experience working as a driver, including at least one year on “C1”. All the conditions are met here. The requirements for category “D” are different: from age 23, with at least one year on “D1”.
